_readme: Gzipped kilobyte budgets for the production bundle, enforced by
Every number was MEASURED before it was written: the values below come from the
build of 2026-10-13 and carry roughly 10-15% headroom. A gate nobody can pass is
a gate somebody deletes, so the headroom is deliberate — but raising one of these
to turn a red run green is the failure mode this file exists to prevent. Raise it
with a reason, in a commit that says what grew and why.
Why gzip: that is what the network carries. Why these five: each one catches a
different mistake, and a metric with no budget is a hard error in the checker, so
adding a measurement forces a decision about it.

initialJs.reason: Entry chunk + its modulepreloads: what a first-time visitor downloads before anything paints. Measured 184.8 kB gzip. Every route pays this — the single number that decides whether the app feels fast on the shop floor's 4G.

entryJs.reason: The entry chunk alone. Measured 83.3 kB gzip. Watching it separately from `initialJs` distinguishes 'we added an eager import' from 'we added a preloaded one'.

totalJs.reason: Every lazily-loaded chunk summed (579 chunks today). Measured 1686.1 kB gzip. No visitor downloads all of it, so this is not a speed budget — it is a growth guard on a dependency that ends up imported everywhere.

largestJs.reason: No single chunk should dominate. Measured 123.8 kB gzip (vendor-three; charts is next at 115.9). A heavier chart, map or 3D library shows up here first, and it is the one place where a version bump can silently double a download.

totalCss.reason: One stylesheet across three files, measured 27.4 kB gzip. Small, and that is the point: the token discipline audit keeps utilities from multiplying, and this catches it if that ever slips.
